title: Generative AI, explained simply
oneliner: Generative AI takes your data as input and produces something new from it - a new route map, a new infrastructure config - instead of just analyzing what exists.
says: Generative AI is the branch of AI where you input data and statistics and it generates new output based on what you provided. His examples: feed a city's transportation data and it generates a new route or map for the transport system; feed infrastructure configuration and metadata and it generates a new cloud infrastructure setup for your applications.
explained: The definition is deliberately plain, and the examples are chosen from his own world. The transport example shows 'generate' means create-a-new-artifact, not summarize-an-old-one. The infrastructure example is the one aimed at his audience: configuration files, architecture diagrams, and deployment scripts are all generatable artifacts, which is why GenAI landed in the architect's toolbox rather than staying a curiosity.

The mental model to carry forward: generative models are pattern completers trained on enormous corpora. Give them enough context about what you want - the data, the metadata, the constraints - and the output quality tracks the input quality. That idea, input context deciding output quality, becomes the entire basis of his RAG and prompt-registry episodes in Season 2.
takeaway: GenAI = new artifacts from your inputs. The quality of what it makes is bounded by the quality of context you feed it.
